questions.topic: Volume against surface area
questions.learningObjective: Explain why volume grows faster than surface area
questions.stem: Memo 7 asks why volume grows faster than surface area when scaling.

answer.exemplar: Volume scales with the cube of the linear factor while surface area scales with the square, so volume outgrows surface area for larger solids as size increases.

questions.explanation: Cubic scaling outpaces squared scaling. This is why large objects have relatively less surface area.

questions.topic: A circumscribed circle and a square
questions.stem: Memo 1 asks which expression gives circumradius of a square side s.

options.text: s divided by 2
s times square root of 2 divided by 2
s squared divided by 2
s times square root of 2
options.misconception: confuses "s times square root of 2" with the correct "s times square root of 2 divided by 2"

questions.explanation: Half the diagonal. Applying it makes "s times square root of 2 divided by 2" correct. The alternative "s divided by 2" is wrong because it uses inradius formula. The key is B, "s times square root of 2 divided by 2". Option A ("s divided by 2") is wrong: uses inradius formula. Option C ("s squared divided by 2") is wrong: squares the side unnecessarily.
